questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You have said that, / as he took money from you many times, / he owes you / five thousand rupees all together.
options: as he took money from you many times
explanation: five thousand rupees all together 'All together' must be replaced with 'altogether', which means totally. Hence, 'five thousand rupees altogether' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I stayed in my hometown with my parents on the pandemic.
explanation: on 'On' is used to indicate a specific occasion or day. 'During' is used to indicate a specific period of time. Similarly, 'pandemic' is a specific period of time. Hence, 'during' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "In August, she will be / enjoying / all the fruits her grandmother / will plant last January.
explanation: will plant last January The phrase 'last January' indicates the use of simple past tense. 'Will plant' must be replaced with the past form 'planted'. Hence, 'planted last January' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: 'The compensation that the '[A] / Government agreed to provide to [B] / the dependents of the [C] / train accident is fairly less [D].
explanation: D- train accident is fairly less 'Less' must be replaced with 'low' as there is no comparison in this sentence. Hence, 'train accident is fairly low' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "(a) The more it rains,/ (b) worse/ (c) the roads become/ No error
explanation: worse 'Worse' must be replaced with 'the worse'. When change in one thing causes the change in the other and two comparative degrees are used to indicate this relationship, it is called successive comparison. Article 'the' is used before both the comparative degrees. Hence, 'the worse' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mr. Unkerton glanced / to the inspector, / who merely snorted / and looked at the ceiling.
explanation: to the inspector 'To' must be replaced with 'at' as we use 'at' with 'glance' for a person. Hence, 'at the inspector' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: 'She spotted the novel '[A] / and shouted, 'Here the book lies [B] / that we were searching for[C] / all around.'[D]
explanation: B - and shouted, "Here the book lies 'That' is a relative pronoun which takes a noun or pronoun as its antecedent. In the given sentence, 'the book' is the antecedent, which will be used before 'that'. Hence, and shouted, "Here lies the book is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Raghu did not get the job / because he did not have / experience enough for the post.
options: Raghu did not get the job
explanation: experience enough for the post 'Enough' is an adjective which describes the noun 'experience', therefore 'enough' will be used before 'experience'. Hence, 'enough experience for the job' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I will have been studying English for three years by the end of this course.
options: I had been studying English for three years by the end of this
I have been studying English for three years by the end of this
I will have been studying English for three years by the end of
I was studying English for three years by the end of this
explanation: I will have been studying English for three years by the end of this course. There is no error in the given sentence. Hence, the sentence given in option(c) is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The police are searching about the missing jewellery.
explanation: about 'For' is the fixed preposition used after the verb 'search'. Hence, 'for' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "John is really / good in/ playing/ the piano.
explanation: good in The structure 'good + at + V ing ' is used to show that you are very skilful and clever at doing something. Hence, 'good at' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The Supreme Court set away / the verdict of the High Court / and agreed to hear the plea / of the complainant.
options: and agreed to hear the plea
the verdict of the High Court
explanation: The Supreme Court set away 'Set away' must be replaced with 'set aside'. The phrasal verb 'set aside' means to deprive of legal effect because it has been proved wrong. The given sentence states that the Supreme Court set aside the verdict of the High Court. Hence, 'The Supreme Court set aside' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mrs. Premlatha asked / Malini to hand down / all the / payment slips.
explanation: Malini to hand down 'Hand down' must be replaced with 'hand out'. The phrasal verb 'hand out' means to give a slip or document to someone. The given sentence talks about giving all the payment slips. Hence, 'Malini to hand out' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "She is / as more intelligent as / her brothers are.
explanation: as more intelligent as 'As + adjective/adverb + as' is a comparative structure in which the adjective or the adverb is always in the positive degree. Therefore, 'more' will be replaced with 'much'. Hence, 'as much intelligent as' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He is waiting / at airport to receive / Mr. Smith, who is / coming from South Africa.
explanation: at airport to receive Article 'the' is used to refer to a specific or particular noun. 'Airport' given in the sentence is specific as the person is waiting there. Hence, 'at the airport to receive' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I hope that / yesterday's lunch / at Rahul's place / was at your liking.
explanation: was at your liking "To one's liking" is the correct phrase, which means appeal able or enjoyable to someone. Therefore, 'at your liking' must be replaced with 'to your liking'. Hence, 'was to your liking' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "She forbade / him not / to enter that / room.
explanation: him not 'Not' must be removed from this sentence. 'Forbade' is the past form of 'forbid', which means to not allow someone to do something. The use of 'not' with 'forbade' is superfluous. Hence, 'forbade him to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He climbed of / the steep mountain trail, / his backpack heavy / with supplies for the journey.
explanation: He climbed of 'Climbed of' must be replaced with 'climbed up'. 'Up' is used to indicate upwards movement. Hence, 'he climbed up' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Sam and Teena / had wondering / what to do this weekend.
explanation: had wondering The given sentence is an example of present continuous tense and the subject 'Sam and Teena' is plural. 'Plural Subject + are + V ing ' is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, 'are wondering' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You know that I am fond of reading / and also that all books are my favourite / but you don't know that this is one of / my favourite book.
options: but you don't know that this is one of
and also that all books are my favourite
You know that I am fond of reading
explanation: my favourite book 'One of + plural noun' is the correct grammatical structure. Therefore, the plural noun 'books' will be used. Hence, 'my favourite books' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that contains a grammatical error from the options below:
options: This is a very difficult task to accomplish.
A young boy offered her his seat.
I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.
I have a lot of work to complete.
explanation: I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life. Article 'an' will be used before the noun 'eraser' as it starts with a vowel sound. Hence, the correct sentence is- 'I wish I had an eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "In addition with / the existing crisis in economy, / the rise of hunger index / is another cause of worry.
explanation: in addition with 'In addition to' is the correct phrase. Hence, 'in addition to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that contains a grammatical error from the options below:
options: She usually walks her dog in the park every morning.
The train leaves the station at 8:00 a.m. every day.
They play chess together on weekends.
explanation: He don't like spicy food. 'The given sentence is in the simple present tense and 'Singular Subject(He) + does + not + V 1 ' is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, the correct sentence is- 'He doesn't like spicy food.' (a) They have an information about the event. 'Information' is an uncountable noun and we generally do not use indefinite articles (a/an) with uncountable nouns. Therefore, 'an' will be removed. Hence, the correct sentence is- 'They have information about the event.

questionText: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
options: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft
An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft
explanation: The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication. 'Dance' and 'cleft' mentioned in the sentence are specific and we generally use the definite article 'the' before a specific or particular noun. The noun 'role' is not specific and we generally use an indefinite article before a non-specific noun. The word 'crucial' starts with a consonant sound, therefore, article 'a' will

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He will have to / knuckle up really seriously, / if he wants to / crack the upcoming deal.
explanation: knuckle up really seriously 'Knuckle up' must be replaced with 'knuckle down'. The phrasal verb 'knuckle down' means to put in serious effort. The given sentence states that he will have to knuckle down really seriously if he wants to crack the upcoming deal. Hence, 'knuckle down really seriously' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
options: A lot of books and notes place in order look most
A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed on order looks most
A lot of book and notes placed in order looks most
explanation: A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating. 'A lot of books and notes' is a plural subject that will take 'look' as a plural verb. The phrase 'in order' means arranged systematically. We can not use the superlative degree of 'fascinating' as there is no comparison with any other thing. Hence, the sentence given in option (b) is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He missed the college bus / because he woke up / unpardonably lately in the .
explanation: unpardonably lately in the morning 'Lately' must be replaced with 'late'. 'Late' means after the usual or expected time. 'Lately' means in the recent times. The given sentence is talking about waking up after the expected time in the morning. Hence, 'unpardonably late in the morning' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "After the match, / the stadium was the messiest / it's ever been.
explanation: No error The given sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Gita got onto / the book / she was reading / this .
explanation: Gita got onto 'Got onto' must be replaced with 'got into'. The phrasal verb 'got into' means became interested in a subject or activity. The given sentence talks about the interest of Gita in the book she was reading. Hence, 'Gita got into' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Although experts are worried / that retail inflation is rising / at a steep rate, / the crisis will soon blow away.
options: the crisis will soon blow away
explanation: the crisis will soon blow away 'Blow away' must be replaced with 'blow over'. The phrasal verb 'blow over' means to pass by or to end. The given sentence states that the crisis will soon end. Hence, 'the crisis will soon blow over' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Select the option that has an error in the use of present tense.
options: The painter is painting the wall right now.
The mother cooks delicious food for her children.
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
I have performed all my duties with utmost sincerity.
explanation: I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour. Present perfect continuous tense will be used in this sentence as a fixed period of time is mentioned with the preposition 'for'. Therefore, 'am observing' must be replaced with 'have been observing'. Hence, the correct sentence is - 'I have been observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.' SSC CGL 10/09/2024 (2nd Shift)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old. / So my mother is old than my uncle.
options: and my uncle is 48 years old.
So my mother is old than my uncle
explanation: So my mother is old than my uncle 'Old' must be replaced with the comparative degree 'older' as the given sentence compares the age of mother and uncle. Hence, 'So my mother is older than my uncle' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "My sister is allergic with peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal
explanation: allergic with peanuts 'To' is the fixed preposition used after the adjective 'allergic'. Hence, 'allergic to peanuts' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that contains a grammatical error from the options below:
options: They have an information about the event.
The cat is sleeping on a mat.
She is an artist at a local gallery.
Can you bring me the keys to the car?
explanation: They have an information about the event. 'Information' is an uncountable noun and we generally do not use indefinite articles (a/an) with uncountable nouns. Therefore, 'an' will be removed. Hence, the correct sentence is- 'They have information about the event.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Whenever she is coming / here, she brings / many gifts for everyone.
explanation: Whenever she is coming 'Whenever' is used when one action is always followed by another action. Simple present tense is used with 'whenever'. 'She' is a singular subject that will take 'comes' as a singular verb. Hence, 'Whenever she comes' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
options: She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes was
She was not allow to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were (alt)
explanation: She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty. 'Singular Subject + was + V 3 ' is the correct passive structure for simple past tense. 'Clothes' is a plural subject that will take 'were' as a plural verb. Hence, the sentence given in option(d) is correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which was landing at 5:00 a.m. yesterday.
explanation: Switzerland by the We generally do not use article 'the' after 'by' when we mention the means of transport such as bus, train, bike, car, flight, etc. Therefore, article 'the' will be removed. Hence, 'Switzerland by' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "(1) We knocked across (2) early on Saturday (3) to enjoy (4) the beautiful weather.
explanation: We knocked across 'Knocked across' must be replaced with the phrasal verb 'knocked off'. 'Knock off' means to stop work. The given sentence states that we stopped work early on Saturday to enjoy the beautiful weather. Hence, 'We knocked off' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He bought strange vintage car on auction from the customs department.
explanation: strange vintage car We generally use an indefinite article (a/an) before a non-specific noun. In the given sentence, the word 'strange' starts with a consonant sound. Therefore, article 'a' will be used. Hence, 'a strange vintage car' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I thought of this idea / just when you called / me yesterday.
explanation: No error The given sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Meenu looks / much better / today.
explanation: No error The given sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mr. Abhilash and his family / have received / no informations / about the incident.
explanation: no informations 'Informations' must be replaced with 'information' as 'information' is an uncountable noun and its plural cannot be formed. Hence, 'no information' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Every students in the hostel decided to travel to Delhi to witness the Republic Day parade.
explanation: Every students in the hostel 'Everyone/each/ every/ nothing/ everything/ anything/ either/ neither' represents a singular noun. Therefore, 'students' must be replaced with the singular noun 'student'. Hence, 'Every student in the hostel' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "By this time next year / I will had graduated from college / and starting my first job / in the field of marketing.
options: I will had graduated from college
explanation: I will had graduated from college 'Subject + will have + V 3 ' is the correct grammatical structure for a sentence which is in the future perfect tense. Therefore, 'will had' must be replaced with 'will have'. Hence, 'I will have graduated from college' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I are dancing with my husband at my sister's wedding.
explanation: I are dancing 'Am' is the correct helping verb to use with 'I' in present continuous tense. Hence, 'I am dancing' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "After the concert was over, / they go to a restaurant, / had dinner together / and talked until midnight.
explanation: they go to a restaurant, The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb in the past form (V 2 ), not the present form (go). Hence, 'they went to a restaurant' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Renewable energy / sources like solar and wind power / will replaced traditional fossil fuels / and help reduce carbon emissions.
options: sources like solar and wind power
explanation: will replaced traditional fossil fuels 'Modal verbs' are auxiliary verbs(also called helping verbs) like can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. However, after a modal verb, we generally use the first form of the verb (V 1 ). Hence, 'will replace(V 1 ) traditional fossil fuels' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "No other place in this country is so better as Gulmarg, Kashmir.
explanation: so better as Positive degree adjective is used in the structure 'as'…as' or 'so'…as' to make a comparison. Therefore, 'better' must be replaced with 'good'. Hence, 'so good as' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Our family is planning / a trip to Europe next summer / where we should visit several famous / landmarks and enjoy local cuisine.
options: where we should visit several famous
a trip to Europe next summer
explanation: where we should visit several famous 'Should' must be replaced with 'will' as the action of visiting several famous landmarks will happen in the future (next summer). Hence, 'where we will visit several famous' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "It is he who work for the company for more than a decade.
explanation: who work 'Who work' must be replaced with 'who has been working' as we use the perfect continuous tense with 'for/since' to indicate time period. Hence, 'who has been working' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The windows / violent banged / during the / storm yesterday.
explanation: violent banged 'Violent' must be replaced with 'violently' as the given sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb 'banged'. Hence, 'violently banged' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law / attended the meeting / as his health is not more good.
options: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law
as his health is not more good
explanation: as his health is not more good 'More' must be removed as we use comparative degree adjective to make a comparison but there is no comparison between the health of two people. The first part of the sentence is in the past tense, so the verb in the second clause will also be in the past tense(V 2 ). Hence, 'as his health was not good' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.
explanation: he is as smarter as 'As + adjective/adverb + as' is a comparative structure in which we always use positive degree. Therefore, 'smarter' must be replaced with 'smart'. Hence, 'he is as smart as' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Solutions to the country's interior problems are still a long way away.
explanation: the country's interior The correct word to use in this sentence is 'internal', not 'interior'. 'Internal' means occurring inside a country. Hence, the country's internal is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
explanation: They secret The given sentence needs an adverb 'secretly' to modify the verb 'decided', not the noun 'secret'. Hence, 'They secretly' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He ran quick to catch the bus.
explanation: quickly The given sentence needs an adverb 'quickly' to modify the verb 'ran', not the adjective 'quick'. Hence, 'quickly' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mrs. Sreelakshmi's / musical intelligence / is superior than / Mrs. Suma's.
explanation: is superior than There are some words that take the preposition 'to' after them. For example:- superior to, inferior to, prior to, elder to, junior to, senior to, etc. Hence 'is superior to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The employees were comfortable / with me and they talked about / their problems since / I has worked there as a manager.
options: I has worked there as a manager.
with me and they talked about
explanation: I has worked there as a manager. The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb of past tense. 'Had' will be used instead of 'has'. Hence, 'I had worked there as a manager' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error. Mr. Arun / will pay dear / for his / financial mistake.
explanation: will pay dear The given sentence needs an adverb 'dearly' to modify the verb 'pay', not the adjective 'dear'. Hence, 'will pay dearly' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "My brother received / his MBA degree into / the university last year.
explanation: his MBA degree into 'Into' must be replaced with 'from' as we use 'from' to indicate the source of something. Hence, 'his MBA degree from' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He replied / in a dry tone, / "Ouch! I will not work / for you anymore.
explanation: Ouch! I will not work 'Ouch!' is used to express pain. However, in the given sentence, the speaker replied in a dry tone. So, the correct interjection to use is 'Ugh!'. Hence, 'Ugh! I will not work for you anymore' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
explanation: have no interior 'Have no interior' must be replaced with 'has no ulterior'. 'Mr. Surya' is a singular subject that will take 'has' as a singular verb. Also, the correct word to use here is 'ulterior'. 'Ulterior motive' means a secret reason for doing something. Hence, 'has no ulterior' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "By the end of / this month, he / will been working / for five years.
explanation: will been working 'Will been' must be replaced with 'will have been'. Future perfect continuous tense (will have been + V ing ) is used to talk about the duration of an action that has happened until some point in the future and will still be happening. Hence, 'will have been working' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
explanation: I have the hundred reasons The reasons given in the sentence are not specific and we use indefinite article for a non-specific noun. Article 'a' will be used as the word 'hundred' begins with a consonant sound. Hence, 'I have a hundred reasons' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "After I retire, I started a second career / as a writer and published several books / which allowed me to share my stories / and insights with a wider audience.
options: and insights with a wider audience
After I retire, I started a second career
as a writer and published several books
which allowed me to share my stories
explanation: After I retire, I started a second career If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V 3 ) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V 2 ). However, the V 3 form of 'retire' is 'retired'. Hence, 'After I had retired (V 3 )' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error. Although the team had trained diligently for months, they had still overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
explanation: had still overwhelmed 'Had' must be replaced with 'were' as the given sentence is an example of a passive voice of simple past tense and 'Plural subject (they) + were + V 3 ' is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, 'were still overwhelmed(V 3 )' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Due to the pandemic, / the prices of / medicines increased / every day since / last December.
explanation: medicines increased We use present continuous tense with 'for/since' to show that something has been happening for a period of time. 'Plural subject (prices) + have been + V ing ' is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, 'medicines have been increasing' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. UNESCO works to / strengthen an intellectual / and moral solidarity / of humankind.
explanation: strengthen an intellectual Indefinite article 'a/an' is not used for an abstract noun(solidarity). The definite article 'the' is used before a specific or particular noun. The given sentence is referring to a specific type of solidarity. Hence, 'strengthen the intellectual and moral solidarity' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour.
explanation: brought about a new 'Brought out' is the correct phrasal verb here, which means 'published'. The given sentence is talking about publishing a new book. Hence, 'brought out a new' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that contains a grammatical error from the options below:
options: It is said that Joseph was not ready to go to war.
Karl Marx was a renowned social scientist.
Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.
It is impossible to wake Christine up in the morning.
explanation: Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity. 'Forces' will be used instead of 'force' according to the plural verb 'are' and the plural adjective 'their'. Hence, the correct sentence is: "Indian forces are known for their loyalty and integrity.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Brr, the city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing!
explanation: Brr An interjection is a word or phrase used to express a sudden feeling. 'Brr' is used to express the sensation of cold. 'Wow' is used to express a sudden feeling of amazement. Hence, 'Wow' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Having known that / the train was already on the platform, / they ran fastly / to catch it.
options: the train was already on the platform
explanation: they ran fastly 'Fast' is already an adverb. The word 'fastly' does not exist. Hence, 'they ran fast' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Deepa and Seema are both good with running, but Deepa is also good at catching the ball and throwing it to the right corner in time.
explanation: good with running Preposition 'at' is used to show that someone is good at doing something. 'Good + at + V ing ' is the correct structure. Hence, 'good at running' is the most appropriate answer. SSC CHSL 02/07/2024 (4th Shift)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "People admired him, for / he lived by the same principals / that he preached.
options: he lived by the same principals
explanation: he lived by the same principals 'Principals' must be replaced with 'principles' as the given sentence talks about a kind of belief or idea that guides you. Hence, 'he lived by the same principles' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "We were on the way/ to the party;/ suddenly, there/ will a heavy downpour.
explanation: will a heavy downpour. The given sentence is in the past tense, not in the future tense, so it must have the verb in the past form 'was',. Hence, 'was a heavy downpour' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He never talks / for anybody. / He is alone / all day.
explanation: for anybody 'To' is used to denote the person to whom someone is talking. Hence, 'to anybody' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The police told the agitators to back in, else they would lathi-charge.
explanation: the agitators to back in 'Back out' is the correct phrasal verb to use here. 'Back out' means to withdraw or decide not to do something that was planned to do. Hence, 'the agitators to back out' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "We took dinner in a Chinese restaurant and were amazed to see the interior of a restaurant.
explanation: the interior of a restaurant Article 'the' is used when we refer to the same noun again because it becomes specific. Hence, 'the interior of the restaurant' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mr. Ali's shop / is further to / the hospital.

options: A celestial body or astronomical object is
or configuration that happens in the visible universe
a naturally occurring physical thing, association
explanation: No error The given sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Select the segment that contains the error, from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. It was A: / by a chance B: / he saw a movie in a theatre C:.
options: / by a chance (B) / he saw a movie in a theatre (C).
/ he saw a movie in a theatre (C).
explanation: By a chance Article 'a' must be removed as 'by chance' is the correct phrase. 'By chance' means accidentally, without plan or intent. Hence, 'by chance' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "One of these / boxes have / the portrait / of the heiress.
explanation: boxes have 'Have' must be replaced with 'has.' According to the "Subject-Verb Agreement Rule", 'One of/ Each of/ Most of/ Either of + Plural Subject + Singular verb' is grammatically the correct structure. Hence, 'boxes has' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You can fool some of the people all the time, and all the Spot the Error people some of the time; but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
options: You can fool some of the people all the time
and all the people some of the time
but you cannot fool all the people all the time.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Hardik's horoscope says / that the stars / will be exercised/ a benign influence on his life.
options: a benign influence on his life
explanation: will be exercised 'Will be exercised' must be replaced with 'will exercise' as we generally use active voice when the subject is the doer of the action. In the given sentence, the subject('stars') is the doer of the action(exercise an influence). Hence, 'will exercise' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I had gone to Siliguri before I go to Raiganj.
explanation: go 'Go' must be replaced with 'went'. If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V 3 ) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V 2 ). Hence, 'went(V 2 )' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "If things were not going to be normal / after the pandemic, mankind will / have to accept the New Normal.
options: have to accept the New Normal
If things were not going to be normal
explanation: If things were not going to be normal 'Were' must be replaced with 'are' as the given sentence is an example of the mixed conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is "If + Present Tense…'….will +V 1 ". Hence 'If things are not going to be normal' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
options: The decision to change a hospital saved an life of the
The decision to change the hospital saved the life of the
The decision to change an hospital saved the life of the
A decision to change a hospital saved the life of the daughter
explanation: The decision to change the hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.(Correct) (a) The decision to change a hospital saved an life of the daughter of the doctor.(Incorrect Article)(c) The decision to change an hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.(Incorrect Article)(d) A decision to change a hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.(Incorrect Article) SSC CHSL 24/05/2022 (Evening)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I am sure that / the postman would be / coming shortly / to deliver the letter.
explanation: the postman would be 'Would be' must be replaced with 'will be'. Modal 'would' is used to talk about the future as seen from the past. Modal 'will' is used to talk about the future as seen from the present moment. As the first part of the sentence is in Present Tense, modal 'will' will be used. Hence, 'the postman will be' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Maruti likes / adventure / stories, especially / an adventures of Tarzan.
explanation: an adventures of Tarzan 'An' must be replaced with 'the. The word "adventures" is plural, so it should not be preceded by the singular article "an". We generally use the definite article with a specific noun or a particular noun (adventures of Tarzan). Hence, 'the adventures of Tarzan' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The historians / are a great / asset to the/ field of academia.
explanation: The historians 'The historians' must be replaced with 'historians' as we generally use definite article 'the' with a specific or particular noun. Here, in the given sentence 'historians' is a common noun. So, we will not use definite articles before 'historians'. Hence, 'historians' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
options: The warrior was waiting for an right time to attack the lion
The warrior was waiting for the right time to attack the lion
An warrior was waiting for a right time to attack the lion
The warrior was waiting for a right time to attack an lion
explanation: The warrior was waiting for the right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave. (Correct) (a) The warrior was waiting for an right time to attack the lion hiding in a cave.(Incorrect Article)(c) An warrior was waiting for a right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave. (Incorrect Article)(d) The warrior was waiting for a right time to attack an lion hiding in the cave. (Incorrect Article)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "We hardly knew nothing / about the manager / who had recently joined.
explanation: We hardly knew nothing 'Nothing' must be replaced with 'anything'. 'Hardly' and 'Nothing' both are negative words so we can't use them together. We generally use the pronoun 'anything' in negative and interrogative sentences. Hence, ' we hardly knew anything' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Anti-party activities / improved my relations /with an opposition.
explanation: With an opposition Article 'An' must be replaced with 'the' as Article 'the' is used to represent a class or group. Hence, 'with the opposition' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You wash / the dishes / and / I dry the same.
explanation: l dry the same 'I dry' must be replaced with 'I will dry' as 'Simple Future Tense(Will + V 1 )' is used when discussing a planned action in the future that is related to a present action. Hence, 'I will dry the same' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
options: It was a hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchases and a
It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and a
It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and an
It was the hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchase and the
explanation: It was a hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchases and a couple of meetings.(Correct)(b) It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and a couple of meetings. (Incorrect Noun)(c) It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and an couple of meetings. (Incorrect Noun)(d) It was the hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchase and the couple of meetings. (Incorrect Article)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "When Mrs. Sinha came to see Varanasi in 2019, Nupur has been living there for five years.
explanation: When Mrs. Sinha came to see Varanasi in 2019, Nupur has already been teaching there for five years. 'Has been' must be replaced 'had been' as the first clause of the sentence is in Past Tense. So, we need to use "Past Perfect Tense(Had been + V 1 -ing)" to make the sentence grammatically correct. Hence, 'Nupur had already been teaching(V 1 - ing)' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "She is in / an hurry / to meet / her brother.
explanation: an hurry 'An hurry' must be replaced with 'a hurry' as article 'A' is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Hence, 'She is in a hurry' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He was always been a grumpy man, so I never liked him.
explanation: He was always been a grumpy man, so I never liked him and avoided his company. 'Was' must be replaced with 'has' in the error part. As "has" is the auxiliary verb used with the past participle "been" to indicate a continuous state from the past to the present. Hence, 'he has always been' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Identify the option that rectifies the error in the given sentence. In 2023, she will has been working in the company for three years.
explanation: she will have been The given sentence is an example of 'Future perfect continuous Tense' and the correct grammatical structure is "Will/shall + have been + V 1 -ing". Hence, 'she will have been' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "They usually allege that there is / a delay in procuring stationery / due to the faulty purchase orders.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "It can / get extreme cold / during / the winters.
explanation: get extreme cold 'Extreme' must be replaced with 'extremely' as the given sentence needs an adverb to modify the adjective(cold). Hence, 'It can get extremely cold' is the most appropriate answer. SSC Selection Post (Phase-XI)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I caught / a white cat / rustling / beneath my room.
explanation: beneath my room There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition 'beneath' must be replaced with 'in' as 'beneath' is used to indicate a location that is below something and 'in' is used to indicate that something is located inside of something else. Hence, 'in my room' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Kids learn / a lot by / their / school activities and homework
explanation: a lot by There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. 'A lot by' must be replaced with 'a lot from' as the preposition 'by' is generally used to indicate the way something is done and the preposition 'from' is used to indicate the source of gaining knowledge. Hence, 'a lot from' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "If you live / in a foreign country,/ you should/ try and learn language.
explanation: try and learn language 'And' must be replaced with 'to' as we generally use an 'to + infinitive(V 1 )' after certain verbs like try, bid, let, make, need etc. Hence, 'try to learn language' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He is as concerned as me / regarding / the renewed / examination schedule.

explanation: He is as concerned as me Pronoun 'Me' must be replaced with 'I' as the conjunction pair "as'….as" is used to do comparison between the same 'Cases of pronoun'. So we need to use the subjective case of pronoun i.e. 'I'. Hence, 'He is as concerned as I' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "After that long , / when I quietly entered her room / to hand over the packet to her, / she asked me to sit reluctant
options: she asked me to sit reluctant
to hand over the packet to her,
when I quietly entered her room
explanation: she asked me to sit reluctant 'Reluctant' must be replaced with 'Reluctantly' as we generally use adverbs to modify or describe verbs(sit). Hence, 'she asked me to sit reluctantly' is the most appropriate answer. SSC CHSL 2022 Tier - 2

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The police could not / hold on the people / for long as they / gathered in large numbers.
explanation: hold on the people 'On' must be replaced with 'back' as the "Hold back" is a phrasal verb that means to stop or prevent someone or something. Hence, 'hold back the people' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The students were / able to get better from / college early so they / went to the movies.
explanation: to get better from 'Better' must be replaced with 'back' as the phrase 'get back' means to return. Hence, 'get back' is the most appropriate answer. SSC MTS 2022 Tier - 1

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The front part is used for carving / the lines and the back end / for scratching of whole areas.
options: the lines and the back end
The front part is used for carving
explanation: for scratching of whole areas Preposition 'of' will be removed as scratch is a transitive verb and it will not use any preposition with it. The will be used before "whole". Hence, 'For scratching the whole areas' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Where can I find / a good Chinese / restaurant about here?
explanation: restaurant about here? 'About' will be removed. 'About' is not needed. Hence, 'restaurant here' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Factoring is, of course, different from and superior than / bill discounting, from the point of / view of a small company
options: bill discounting, from the point of
Factoring is, of course, different from and superior than
explanation: Factoring is, of course, different from and superior than 'Than' will be replaced by 'to' as we generally use the preposition 'to' with some Adjectives for comparison (Similar, Superior, Inferior, Equal, Identical). Hence, 'Factoring is, of course, different from and superior to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Now its referring to the same / big lug who met his fate / thanks to David's slingshot.
options: big lug who met his fate
Now its referring to the same
explanation: Now its referring to the same It's is a contraction and should be used where a sentence would read "it is." Its with no apostrophe is the possessive pronoun, like "his" and "her," for nouns without gender. Hence, ' Now it's referring to the same ' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Much of the art he/ discusses is funny, playing / and mischievous.
explanation: discusses is funny, playing 'Playing' must be replaced with 'playful' as we need to use a predicative adjective : These adjectives come after linking verbs (e.g., "be," "become," "seem") and describe the subject of the sentence. Hence, 'discusses is funny, playful' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error' The police released a statement saying, / "This was one of the most vicious/ attack we have ever seen.
options: The police released a statement saying,
This was one of the most vicious
explanation: attack we have ever seen. "One of the + Superlative degree of the adjective(best, worst, etc) + Plural Subject" is grammatically the correct structure. For example, one of the best men, one of the greatest kings, one of the worst phones, etc. Hence, 'attacks we have ever seen' is the most appropriate structure.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Why is your friend / giving me / weird looks?

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "To treat nightmare disorder, / there is a number / of medications and therapies.
explanation: there is a number 'Is' must be replaced with 'are' in the given sentence. According to the subject-verb agreement, 'A + Number of + Plural nouns' always takes plural verbs. Hence, 'there are a number' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "It is believed that / difficult tasks demand lot / of our resources.
explanation: difficult tasks demand lot We generally use article 'a' with 'lot' as an expression meaning 'a larger quantity' or 'many' (a lot of books, a lot of experience). Hence, 'difficult tasks demand a lot' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Your ears are itching / because you are having an / allergic reaction.
explanation: No error The sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Don't you get / involve!' Sandhya / whispered urgently to him.
explanation: involve!' Sandhya 'Involve' must be replaced with 'Involved' in the given sentence. As we generally use past participles with the verb 'get'. Hence, 'involved!' Sandhya' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Never put of / until tomorrow what / you can do today.
explanation: Never put of 'Of' must be replaced with 'off' as the phrasal verb 'put off' means to delay doing something. Hence, 'never put off' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "India is already the third-largest / aviation market in / terms of domestic travel.
explanation: No error The sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Shapes that are impossible / to make of machining / can be printed.
explanation: to make of matching The preposition 'of' must be replaced with 'by' in the given sentence. The use of the preposition 'by' is correct because it is indicating the method by which the shapes are made. While the preposition 'of' is used to indicate a part of something. Hence, 'to make by matching' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The Gryffindors trooped back up / to the castle, none of them talking; / it have been another long day.
options: it have been another long day.
to the castle, none of them talking;
explanation: it have been another long day. 'Have' must be replaced with 'has' in the given sentence. According to the subject-verb agreement, a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. Here, in the sentence 'it' is a singular subject. Hence, 'it has been another long day' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Our passage across the Arabian Sea / was smooth as the most timid of / navigators could desire.
options: Our passage across the Arabian Sea
was smooth as the most timid of
explanation: was smooth as the most timid of Conjunction 'as' will be replaced with 'as...as'. The conjunction 'as' is used to state the reason whereas the conjunction 'as...as' is used to state similarity between two things or situations. The given sentence states the similarity of smoothness between the passage and the desires of the most timid navigator. Hence, 'as smooth as the most timid' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "When I have arrived at / the theatre, the show / had already started.
explanation: When I have arrived at If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V 3 ) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V 2 ). Hence, 'when I arrived at' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Professor Murli's eyebrows / rose a little higher and his / gaze became distinctly coldest.
options: rose a little higher and his
explanation: gaze became distinctly coldest 'Coldest' must be replaced by 'colder' as to maintain consistency, the correct usage would be to use the comparative degree throughout the sentence. In this correction, both "higher" and "colder" are in the comparative degree, indicating a comparison between two states or levels. Hence, 'gaze became distinctly colder' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Early, during December 2021,/ Lal was appointed as / the Secretary to the Lokpal.
explanation: Early, during December 2021 The error in the sentence is the use of the word "during." Since the sentence specifies December 2021, it implies that Lal was appointed as the Secretary to the Lokpal at some point within that month. However, the word "during" suggests a continuous action or a period of time, which is not appropriate in this context. Hence, 'Early in december 2021' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew / its top, burying the ancient / cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
options: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew
explanation: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew Article 'the' must be removed as we generally use article 'the' with the names of mountains but we do not use 'the' if the name includes Mount or Mountain (Mount Olympus, Brokeback Mountain).

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I hope that / we will arrive at / the ideal trade-off soon.
explanation: No error The sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "If I was a clown, / I would have made / everyone smile.
explanation: If I was a clown, 'Was' must be replaced with 'Were'. When expressing unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future, the subjunctive mood is used, which requires the use of 'were' instead of 'was' after 'if'. Hence, 'If I were a clown' is the most appropriate answer. SSC MTS 02/11/2021 (Morning)

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Peoples might confess / just to get out of / the interrogation room.
explanation: Peoples might confess 'Peoples' must be replaced with 'people' as people is already the plural form and it doesn't require 's' to make its plural form. Hence, 'people might confess' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Many female mammals, / including rabbits and cats, ovulate / only when they mate.
explanation: No error The sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "It'd be really cool if you got / on the team, I've never seen you / played badminton, are you good?
options: on the team, I've never seen you
It'd be really cool if you got
explanation: played badminton, are you good? 'Played' must be replaced with 'play' as we generally use bare infinitives after the verbs such as let, bid, see, hear, watch, observe, etc. Hence, 'play badminton, are you good' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The kids there were so notorious, the / more I asked them to quiet down, / the more loud they would scream.
options: the more loud they would scream.
more I asked them to quiet down,
The kids there were so notorious, the
explanation: the more loud they would scream. The phrase 'the more loud' will be replaced with the correct comparative degree 'the louder'. Hence, 'the louder they would scream' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The Federalists wished to / make the central government / as strong possible.
explanation: as strong possible. 'As strong possible' will be replaced with ' as strong as possible'. This is because "As...as" is a comparative structure that shows similarity or equality between two elements. It is used to compare two things or actions and indicates that they are of the same degree or level. Hence, 'as strong as possible' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Can you please / help me to / this project?
explanation: help me to 'Help me to' will be replaced with 'help me with' as the verb "help" is typically followed by the preposition "with" when indicating assistance or support in accomplishing a task or project. Hence, 'Help me with' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He belted two huge sixers, but / eleven to get of the last two / deliveries was a big ask.
options: eleven to get of the last two
explanation: eleven to get of the last two 'Get of' will be replaced with 'Get off' as it means to successfully complete or achieve. It conveys the intended meaning that eleven runs were needed to successfully complete the last two deliveries. Hence, 'Get off' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Can you please / pass me that / glittery pen black?
explanation: glittery pen black? Adjectives should be written before the noun (pen) that is being qualified. The general order of adjectives before a noun is the following: Opinion, Size, Shape, Condition, Age, Colour, Pattern, Origin, Material and Purpose. 'Glittery' represents opinion and 'black' is the color. Hence, 'glittery black pen' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Before he could devote many more / thought to the matter, Pranav / had stepped up to him.
options: Before he could devote many more
explanation: Before he could devote many more 'Many more' will be replaced with 'much more' as much is used to describe the quantity of an uncountable noun. The word "thought" is an uncountable noun, which means it cannot be used with 'many'. Hence, 'before he could devote much more' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I spend a lot of / my time at work helping my / customers find an best outfit.
options: my time at work helping my
explanation: customers find an best outfit. 'An' will be replaced with 'the' as the adjective 'best' is the superlative degree of 'well' and we generally use definite articles with superlative degrees. Hence, 'customers find the best outfit' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "When he buckled down to his / work he became the slyer / and cleverest of diplomats.
options: When he buckled down to his
explanation: work he became the slyer 'The slyer' will be replaced with 'the slyest' as 'slyer' is a comparative form and we need a superlative form of the adjective 'sly' i.e. 'slyest' to match the later part of the sentence. Hence, 'Work he became the slyest' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Neither teahers or / the principal revolted against / the new education policy
explanation: Neither teachers or 'Neither teachers or' will be replaced with 'neither teachers nor' as 'neither….nor' is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, 'Neither teachers nor' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "George handing the / hairpin to Ron, / a moment later.
explanation: George handing the The use of verb 'handing' is incorrect here because we can not use V₄(ing) as the main verb without a helping verb. The adverb 'later' indicates something happened after some time. 'Handing' will be replaced with the past form 'handed' to make it grammatically correct. Hence, 'George handed the' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Humans have rapidly / changing the balance of / gases in the atmosphere.
explanation: changing the balance of The verb 'changing' is incorrect because we can not use 'V 4 '(ing form) with the helping verb of present perfect tense(has/have). The third form (V 3 ) 'changed' will be used in place of 'changing'. Hence, 'changed the balance of' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Largest farmers usually / have more money, social power / and local influence.
explanation: Largest farmers usually 'Largest farmers' will be replaced with 'the largest farmers' as when referring to a specific group of farmers, the definite article 'the' is required before the superlative adjective 'largest'. Hence, 'the largest farmers usually' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I want all / the culprits to / be punished immediate.
explanation: be punished immediate. Adjective 'Immediate' must be replaced with the adverb 'immediately' as we need an adverb to modify the verb 'punished'. Hence, 'to be punished immediately' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You can find these / books into the extreme / corner of this shelf.
explanation: books into the extreme 'Into' will be replaced with 'in' as the preposition 'in' indicates the location of the books. Hence, 'books in the extreme' will be the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mothers can pass the HIV virus to / their newborns during delivery / as well, WHO says.
options: Mothers can pass the HIV virus to
explanation: Mothers can pass the HIV virus to Article 'the' must be removed as we don't use article 'the' before names. 'HIV' is the name of a virus. Hence, 'Mothers can pass HIV virus to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "And how amorous you become / when your courtship with the / muses is going stronger.
explanation: Muses is going stronger 'Muses is' will be replaced with 'muses are'. According to the "Subject-Verb Agreement Rule", a plural subject (muses) always takes a plural verb(are). Hence, 'Muses are going stronger' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Tax dispute settlement / might not work out in / the desired scale.
explanation: might not work out in Preposition 'In' must be replaced with 'on' as we generally use 'on' to discuss the success or outcome of a particular activity or process. Hence, 'might not work out in' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The benefits of rebuilding / healthy, fertile soil / are clear.

explanation: since six months 'For' refers to a specific period of time or a numerical value of time, for example for 2 years, for 4 weeks, for 3 days, etc. However, in the given question, the period of time is 6 months. Hence, 'for six months' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The policeman asked / many people but / no one was knowing / how the accident happened.
explanation: no one was knowing The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its past form(V 2 ) and not in the past continuous form(was +V-ing). Hence, 'no one knew(V 2 )' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "This question / is quite too / simple for me / to answer.
explanation: is quite too The use of 'quite' is irrelevant in the grammatical context of the given sentence as 'too…to' is a fixed pair. Hence, 'is too simple for me to answer' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The manager said, "Could you please confirm me whether you have received all the items that you had ordered?
explanation: confirm me whether you The use of the pronoun 'me' is grammatically incorrect in the given sentence so it must be removed. Hence, 'confirm whether you' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "We thought / there was a good idea / to wear snow boots / before we stepped out.
explanation: there was a good idea 'Idea' in the given sentence is a singular subject and for it, we will use 'it' as a singular pronoun and not 'there'. Hence, 'it was a good idea' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "There have been /three breaks-in /in our society/ this month.
explanation: three breaks-in 'Break-in' is a phrasal verb which means to enter a building by force, usually in order to steal something. However, the given sentence talks about three attempts so we will use the plural form of 'break-in'. Hence, 'three break-ins' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The Taj Mahal / is one of / the most beautiful / creation in the world.
explanation: creation in the world According to the " Subject-Verb Agreement Rule ", ' One of/ Each of/ Most of/ None of + Plural Subject" is grammatically the correct structure. Similarly, the given sentence will have 'creations' as a plural subject. Hence, 'creations in the world' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "This park is / the largest bird sanctuary / in the State.
explanation: No error.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I was angry / on myself / for making / such a silly mistake.
explanation: on myself 'Angry with someone' is grammatically the correct phrase for the given sentence. Hence, 'angry with myself' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market
explanation: two dozens We never write 'dozens' if we are using a numerical amount like two, three, etc. before it. For example, 'two dozens of bananas' is incorrect but 'three dozen of mangoes' is correct. Similarly, the given sentence has 'two' as a numerical value. Hence, 'two dozen' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You and I / have submitted / your work / on time.
explanation: your work 'Our' is the possessive form of 'we' and it means something belonging to us(more than a single person). Similarly in the given sentence, the work belongs to both the persons and not to a single person. Hence, 'our work' is the most appropriate structure.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?
explanation: for walking When we use verbs like walk, talk, ride, drink, etc. as nouns, we put the indefinite article 'a' before them as per their sound. For example, we had a talk, let's go for a drive, etc. Hence, 'for a walk' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
explanation: Among you and me We use 'among' for more than two persons and 'between' for two persons. However, there are two persons mentioned in the given sentence. Hence, 'Between you and me' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I find that / I get myself tired / very easily / these days.
explanation: I get myself tired The use of the reflexive pronoun 'myself' is irrelevant according to the grammatical context of the sentence so it will be removed. Hence, 'I get tired' is the most appropriate answer. SSC CGL 2020 Tier - 2

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "If you have / remained calm / you could have / saved the situation.
explanation: If you have If you have " If + had + V 3 …. could have + V 3 ( third form of the verb )" is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, 'If you had' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I will spend / my rest of remaining / life in my / native village.
explanation: my rest of remaining We cannot use 'rest' & 'remaining' together in a sentence as it becomes the case of superfluous ness(not necessary). Hence, 'remaining' will be removed from the sentence & 'the rest of my life' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "This dog seems / to be very ferocious, / otherwise, / it is harmless.
explanation: Otherwise 'Otherwise' is a conjunction that means apart from that. However, 'But' is also a conjunction that is used for introducing an idea that contrasts with or is different from what has just been said. Similarly in the given sentence, the statement that the dog is harmless contrasts with its characteristic of being ferocious(violent). Hence, 'But' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The girl lay down / on the bed / besides her mother / and went to sleep.
explanation: besides her mother 'Besides' means 'in addition to something' & 'Beside' means 'at the side of, or next to somebody/something'. However, the given sentence states that the girl lay down on the bed next to her mother and went to sleep. Hence, 'beside her mother' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He went / to the bed / with a / slight fever.
explanation: to the bed We generally use the phrases 'go to bed', 'gone to bed' or 'went to bed'. Hence, we will remove the definite article 'the' from the given sentence and 'went to bed' becomes the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The city turned out / to be very / different to what / he had expected.
explanation: different to what There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition 'to' after 'different' must be replaced with 'from' because 'different' generally takes the preposition 'from' with it. Hence, 'different from what' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Your name / precedes before / mine / in the list.
explanation: precedes before We cannot write 'precedes' and 'before' together in a sentence as they have similar meanings '& that will become a case of superfluous ness (not necessary). Hence, 'before' must be removed from the sentence to make it grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You should / avail this opportunity / to demonstrate / your skills.
explanation: avail this opportunity 'Avail' always takes the preposition 'of' and a reflexive pronoun(myself, yourself, ourselves, etc.) in accordance with the given subject(You). Hence, 'avail yourself of this opportunity' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He was unable / to help me because / he had been failed / to arrange the money.
explanation: he had been failed The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its simple past form(failed) and not in the past perfect form(had been failed). Hence, 'he failed' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "He often / persists to ask / awkward questions / at the board meetings.
explanation: persists to ask " Persist + in + V-ing " is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, the preposition 'to' must be replaced with the preposition 'in' and 'persists in asking(V-ing)' becomes the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Either of these / two roads / lead to / the post office.
explanation: lead to According to the " Subject-Verb Agreement Rule ", ' Either of/ Neither of + Plural Subject + Singular verb ' is grammatically the correct structure. The given sentence has 'Roads' as a plural subject and 'leads' as a singular verb. Hence, 'leads to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "His father / prevented him / to go abroad / for higher studies.
explanation: to go abroad We generally use the preposition 'from' with prevent not 'to'. Hence, we will replace 'to' with 'from' and 'from going abroad' becomes the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "What is the name / of the Swami / whom autobiography / impressed you so much?
explanation: whom autobiography 'Whom' is an object pronoun that refers to the person who was the recipient of an action. However, 'Whose' is a possessive pronoun that refers to the person to whom something belongs. Similarly, the given sentence refers to a Swami to whom the autobiography belongs. Hence, 'whose autobiography' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The crowd of the migrant worker at the station for the Shramik Special is unforgettable.
explanation: of the migrant worker 'Crowd' means a large number of people in one place and these people are migrant workers(not a single worker) in the given sentence. However, it is irrelevant to use the definite article 'the' as the workers are not specific. Hence, 'of migrant workers' is the most appropriate answer. SSC MTS 2020 Tier - 1

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Will you / listen me / when I tell you / the details?
explanation: listen me There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition 'to' is missing after 'listen'. Hence, 'listen to me' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The crow held back / to the piece / of bread / with its claws.
explanation: The crow held back 'Held back' means to not do something & 'held on' means to maintain a grasp on something. Both are phrasal verbs. Similarly, in the given sentence, the crow grasps the piece of bread with its claws. Hence, 'the crow held on' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The farmer is / cutting the corn / which has ripen / in the fields.
explanation: which has ripen 'Has + V 3 ' is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. However, the V 3 form of 'ripen' is 'ripened'. Hence, 'has ripened' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Obi wanted / to continue on / his idea of / building a modern school.
explanation: to continue on There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. Use the preposition 'on' in place of 'with'. Hence, 'to continue with' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "I was watching a whole scene very carefully.
explanation: a whole scene The subject 'whole scene' is specific & before specific or particular nouns, we use the definite article 'the'. Hence, 'the whole scene' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Who has distributed these sweets among the children?
explanation: No error. The given sentence is grammatically correct.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Mr. Choudhri goes to fly to Germany and France next weekend.
explanation: Mr. Choudhri goes The given sentence talks about a future action(next weekend),. The structure 'is going to' is generally used for future actions. Hence, 'Mr. Choudhri is going to' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "Not get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "The man we met was any other than the original owner of the house.
explanation: was any other The phrase 'any other' will be replaced with 'different' which means not the same person. Hence, 'was different than' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: "You can meet me always you like," our teacher told us.
