questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "My new shoes gave me a blistered on my right heel.
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple present tense so the verb must be used in the simple present form(V 1 ). Hence, 'me a blister(V 1 )' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "I can't concentrate on my work because I am thinking off that beautiful scene.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition 'off' must be replaced with 'about' as we generally use the preposition 'about' after the noun 'thinking'. Hence, 'I am thinking about' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Select the option that will improve the (bracketed) part of the sentence. In case of no improvement select the option 'No improvement'. Check all radiators for (meagre leaks, special) round pipework connections.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The early flight is the lest expensive.
explanation: Superlative degree adjective' denotes the form of an adjective that expresses the highest or a very high degree of quality of a thing, person, etc. For example, best, worst, greatest, most, least, etc. However, we always place the definite article 'the' before any superlative adjective. Similarly, in the given sentence, 'least' is the superlative degree adjective. Hence, 'the least expensive' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'. Nonetheless, (many an old poets, such as Tennyson and Browning, has) kept their romances to the end.
options: many old poets, such as Tennyson and Browning, have
many old poets, such Tennyson and Browning, has
many a old poets, such Tennyson and Browning, has
explanation: According to the " Subject-Verb Agreement Rule ", a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, 'poets' is a plural subject that will take 'have' as a plural verb. Hence, 'many old poets, such as Tennyson and Browning, have' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "His shoes were soaked from walk through the dew. Sentence Improvement
explanation: Preposition + V - ing' is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, 'soaked from walking(V - ing)' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "But what of the young people whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of who are presumably born in England?
options: who are part of the cricket crowds, some of who are
whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are
who are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are
explanation: If the relative pronoun is followed by a 'verb', then the relative pronoun must be 'who' and if it is followed by a noun or pronoun, then the relative pronoun must be 'whom'. Hence,'who are(verb) part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "There has been a noticeable fall in the number of children dying from malnutrition.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Dad said that, "She would have been a great sister if she was just a bit more careful".

She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit
She would have been a greatest sister if she was just a bit
explanation: If + Subject + Plural Verb' is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, 'She would have been a great sister if she(subject) were(plural verb) just a bit more careful ' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The number of women working outside homes has been steady increasing.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb(steadily) to modify the verb(increasing) and not an adjective(steady). Hence, 'has been steadily increasing' is the most appropriate answer. SSC CGL 2022 Tier - 2

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Edward II is tragic than some other plays by the dramatist.
explanation: The adjective in the sentence is tragic. The adjective will be used in the comparative form. To make the comparative of tragic we will add "less" before it. Hence, 'less tragic than' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Bloomberg Businessweek is not more popular than some other business magazines in the US.
explanation: No substitution required. The given sentence is grammatically correct. SSC CGL 2022 Tier - 1

explanation: looking for his book There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition 'into' used after the verb 'looking' is incorrect '& it must be replaced with the correct preposition 'for' because 'looking for' which means to search something is the correct phrase. Hence, 'looking for his book' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Pintu has been advised to reduce smoking by his family doctor.
explanation: cut down. 'Cut down' is a phrase that means to reduce the size, amount, or quantity of something. Similarly, the given sentence states that Pintu has been advised to reduce smoking by his family doctor. Hence, 'cut down' is the most appropriate answer.

explanation: yesterday. 'An adverb of time' can tell us about when an action happens. Moreover, late, tomorrow, today, everyday, weekly, yearly, yesterday, last month, tonight, last week, immediately, etc. are some adverbs of time. Similarly, the given sentence is in the past tense(went), and for that, we will use an adverb of time in the past tense. Hence, 'yesterday' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The new shop that opened last week are hardly sufficient stock of the products that it advertised about.
explanation: hardly had. According to the Rule of Inversion, the verb always be used after the adverbs like Hardly, Scarcely, Barely. Hence, 'hardly had(verb)' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Last before year, Shirley got very good grades.
explanation: The year before last 'The year before last' means during the year before the previous one. The given sentence states that Shirley got very good grades in the year before the previous one. Hence, 'The year before last' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Oscar is the most prestigious award which is introduced to good actors in that year.
explanation: awarded to best. Oscars are 'awards' which are generally awarded and not introduced. Moreover, we will use a superlative degree adjective(best) for the actors getting the award. Hence, 'awarded to best' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Select the sentence with the appropriate use of the adverb of frequency.
options: Radha goes to Nagpur with great affection.
Radha goes to Nagpur for her office work.
Radha goes to Nagpur to meet her uncle.
explanation: Radha often goes to Nagpur. An adverb of frequency is a word that can be placed after the noun or pronoun in a sentence to give more information about the verb, adjective or another adverb. Some examples of adverbs of frequencies are rarely, often, always, never and sometimes. Similarly, 'often' as an adverb of frequency is perfectly used in option 'c'. Hence, 'Radha often goes to Nagpur' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Rita will never have changed her job if she would have been promoted.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Santa Claus stays at the North Pole when he isn't out deliver gifts for Christmas.
explanation: Out delivering. "Preposition(out) + V-ing" is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, 'out delivering(V-ing)' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The intern should take a right choice in choosing the right job for her.
explanation: make a right choice. We generally use the verb 'make' with choice and not 'take'. Hence, the correct phrase for the given sentence is 'make a right choice' that means to make the right decision.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Old people acquire experience through age.
explanation: gain experience. We generally use the verb 'gain' before experience and not 'acquire'. The given sentence is a fact so simple present tense will be used. Hence, 'gain experience' is the correct phrase.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.

in means of rope ladders they scaled the wall.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The MNC is about to be bankrupt, according to reliable sources.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Computers and mobile phones have become a necessary and important part of our lives.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Many companies displaced playing income tax last year.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Blind by a dust storm, they fell into disorder.

Similarly, in the given sentence, 'blinded' will be the past participle and the phrase that it governs is 'blinded by a dust storm'. Hence, 'Blinded' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "He was not able to adopt himself to the new environment of the hostel.
explanation: Able to adapt himself to 'Adopt' means to accept or start to use something new and 'Adapt' means to change yourself or something according to conditions. questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "You must aware of friends who speak against you.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The percentage of employees who called in sick and the number of employees who left their jobs within 2 years (were reflective of the level of job satisfaction).

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "As Simon had already been to the park, he lead the way for the other children.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Between Raima and Saima, the former is intelligent, while the latter is beautiful.

explanation: As its (It's) is a contraction of the words it and is/has and 'Its' is the possessive form of the pronoun 'It' which is used to refer to the noun 'Car'. Hence, 'As its' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "He is a weak student and somehow pulled over the exams.
explanation: Pulled through 'Pulled through' is a phrase that means to succeed in surviving a difficult period. The given sentence states that he is a weak student and somehow succeeded to survive/pass the exams. Hence, 'pulled through' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The story did not go by well enough.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "How did you come about his purse?
explanation: Come by 'Come by' is a phrase that means to manage to acquire or obtain something. The given sentence talks about acquiring a purse. Hence, 'come by' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article:
options: An amateur is a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure.
A amateur is a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure.
An amateur is an person who takes part in an activity for pleasure.
Amateur is a person who takes part in a activity for pleasure.
explanation: We generally use the indefinite article 'a' before the words starting with a consonant sound and article 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound. Similarly, in the given sentence, 'noun', 'person', 'hobby', 'job' are some words that are starting with a consonant sound & 'activity' is the only word that starts with a vowel sound. Hence, 'Amateur' is a noun which refers to a person who takes part in an activity as a hobby or for pleasure and not as a job' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "She paid a high price for the clothes she brought at the boutique.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "His last trip around the world taking a toll on his health.
explanation: took a toll The given sentence is in the past tense(last trip) so the verb must be used in the past form(V2) and not in the V-ing form. Hence, 'took(V2) a toll' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Football fans are feeling proud of their teams when they win.

explanation: The given sentence is in the simple present tense so the verb must be used in the simple present form(V1) and not in the present continuous form(are + V-ing). Hence, 'feel(V1) proud of their teams' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The child felt down from a great height.
explanation: Felt' is used to say how something seems to you when you touch, see, smell, experience, etc. it & 'Fell' means to drop down towards the ground. However, the given sentence states that the child fell down from a great height. Hence, 'child fell down' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The application of the medicine seemed to lesson his pain.
explanation: Lesson' means a period of time when you learn or teach something '& 'Lessen' means to make something smaller or less in amount or degree. However, the given sentence states that the application of the medicine seemed to make his pain less. Hence, 'lessen' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The flames of the fire leap into the air.
explanation: leapt into We will use the past form(V2) of the verb 'leap' as the event had occurred in the past. Hence, 'leapt(V2)' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "With tear eyes, she said goodbye to her dear friend.
explanation: Teary eyes' is a phrase that means having eyes that are wet with tears. The given sentence states that she said goodbye to her dear friend with eyes that are wet with tears. Hence, 'teary eyes' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Covid- 19 pandemic has resulted in (an slow change in flowing of capital) generated by workers.

a sluggish change in the flow of capital
an abrupt change in the flow of capital
an sudden change to flow of capital

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The apple tree was loaded of fruit.
explanation: Laden with 'Laden' means heavily loaded with something. The given sentence states that the apple tree was laden (heavily loaded) with fruits. Hence, 'Laden with' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Nobody was interested in the fish who Gopal had catch from the river.
explanation: Which Gopal had caught 'Who' must be replaced with 'Which' as 'Which' is used for things and 'Who' is used for people. Also, we generally use (V 3 ) with had/has/have. Hence, 'Which Gopal had caught' is the most appropriate answer.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "You can have a comfortable journey only then you are getting your seats reserved in advance.
explanation: Only if you get We use the preposition 'If' in conditional sentences. The first conditional sentences are used to express situations in which the outcome is likely to happen in the future and is always used in simple present tense. questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "It is quite difficult to make on what this doctor writes.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Whom was the p erson that you wanted me to contact there?

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Do I need finish this work today itself?

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Is this the same book like our teacher recommended?

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Megha's habit of procrastination puts her colleagues on lot of trouble.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "It is the true fact that the second wave of Covid-19 that has gripped India is more deadly.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "He felt dejected but the feeling passed out in a minute.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The magistrate acquitted him of all charges and set him free.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Why did you take this toy along the child?

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Once Birbal was forbidden for attending the king's free lunch.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The strong wind blow off all the candles.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "After the old building was pulled out, the building contractor surveyed the progress of the work.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "What a palace home!

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The workers' union has threatened for going to an indefinite strike.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "He lost his heart because he could not cope with the difficult situation.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "His fine voice has never heard in this hall again.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "What kind of the book do you want?

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "The porter denied to take the money.

questionText: Select the option that improves the sentence: "Every year the family goes for a pilgrim to the temple at Tirupati.
